clue.text: Arrive, meeting heads of free trade zone then returning recent visitor

parts.note: to arrive is to come

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the string is read backwards
the head of each word is its front, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of free, trade and zone
the first letter of then, read with the others before turning

explanation.surface: A trader turns up at a free trade zone and heads home again.
explanation.walkthrough: COME is followed by F, T, Z, T turned round. Comet C/2022 E3 (ZTF), named after the Zwicky Transient Facility that found it, passed Earth in early 2023 for the first time in about 50,000 years.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet swinging past the Sun is a visitor from the outer solar system, and this one called by only recently.

clue.text: Check with a knight on board — like something out of Chess?

indicators.note: placed on top of in a down entry, so the earlier letters sit above the later ones

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight
a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a festive board

explanation.surface: A chess move: putting a king in check with a knight, which is exactly what happens in chess.
explanation.walkthrough: Every chess term in the clue is a decoy: italic Chess is the stage musical by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters, so something out of it is a song that can be sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs from a musical are made to be sung aloud together, so anything from that show is fit for chanting.

clue.text: Gloom finally obliterated by downpour — it's a plague

indicators.note: the final part is wiped out, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: murk is gloom, here losing its last letter
a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: A dreary day ends with a cloudburst so bad it feels like a biblical plague.
explanation.walkthrough: MURK loses its K and is followed by RAIN. 'Finally' looks like it picks out the last letter of gloom (M), but here it removes one instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old word for an infectious disease of cattle, and more loosely for any pestilence, as in 'a murrain on you'.

clue.text: Sweet soy curd: meal never finished

indicators.note: a thing never finished stops short of its end, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: tofu is soy bean curd, cut short
a feed is a meal, cut short

explanation.surface: A vegan dessert of sweetened tofu, left half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFU and FEED each drop their last letter; the one deletion signal serves both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter, so it counts as a sweet or candy.

clue.text: Hard Lefties upset by being included in time-honoured series

indicators.note: to be included in something is to sit inside it
something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written
the multiplication sign, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Hardline left-wingers are dismayed to find themselves in some old-fashioned series of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is the multiplication sign, as in six by four, and it sits in the middle of the shuffled letters. Lefties looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The X-Files is the American science-fiction television drama that ran from 1993 with revivals into 2018, a long-standing show.

clue.text: I moon and girl turns round

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's large moons

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone moons about while a girl spins round, a dreamy romantic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter I is the definition, not part of the wordplay: it is the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the symbol for the halogen element number 53 on the periodic table, used as an antiseptic.

clue.text: Reserve forwards having treatment to reduce swelling

parts.note: reserve means coolness of manner, as does ice
the forwards in rugby are collectively the pack

explanation.surface: Substitute rugby forwards getting physio for their bruises on the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve and forwards both look like squad positions; one is coolness of manner and the other the rugby scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of crushed ice or a frozen gel pad is held against an injury to cool it and bring inflammation down.

clue.text: Tricksy Medea's daughter takes on tragic heroine

indicators.note: something tricksy plays tricks and is not what it seems, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive S
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: The scheming daughter of Medea, the sorceress of Greek myth, takes on the role of a doomed heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDEAS plus D are rearranged and ON is slipped in: DESDEM, ON, A. Medea is herself a tragic heroine, which makes her look like the answer's source rather than mere letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is Othello's wife in Shakespeare's play, murdered by her husband in the final act.

clue.text: Record melody underpinning New World — 27's

indicators.note: to underpin is to support from below, so in a down entry this piece comes last

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an EP is an extended-play record
a melody is a tune

explanation.surface: A record with a melody beneath the New World Symphony, Dvořák's famous work.
explanation.walkthrough: New World looks like Dvořák's symphony, but New gives N and World begins the definition. 27-across is TRITON, the largest moon of this planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the planet that Triton orbits, so it is the world belonging to that moon.

clue.text: Display cut flower

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Aire in Yorkshire, cut short

explanation.surface: A florist puts cut flowers on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river, one that flows; the Aire runs through Leeds in Yorkshire, and losing its E it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To air views or clothes is to put them out in public, so the verb means show or exhibit.

clue.text: Penny's sheer fun, cavorting in showers, perhaps

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: P for penny, with the possessive S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Penny is having a whale of a time dancing about in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Showers looks like a plural noun of weather, but it is a verb: she showers. 'Perhaps' marks it as one example of freshening up.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a shower is one way of washing and making yourself feel clean again, so it is an example of the phrase.

clue.text: Spooner's 24-hour low period in Exchange

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
a trough is a low point in a cycle
swap the start sounds: the TR of the second word moves to the front of the first

explanation.surface: A daily slump in trading on the stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: A DAY TROUGH becomes TRA-DAY OFF when the TR sound moves to the front and the first word's empty start goes to the back. Exchange looks like the Stock Exchange, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-off is a compromise in which one benefit is given up to gain another, a swap or bargain.

clue.text: Route from a finally snuffed-out Planet Earth

indicators.note: the final light is snuffed out, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
Venus the planet, without its last letter
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: An escape route away from an extinguished, dying Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Planet Earth reads as one phrase, but the two words split: one is Venus shortened, the other its standard letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road or a way of approach, so it serves as a synonym for a route.

clue.text: Rock star Moon obviously round the twist and not all there

indicators.note: twisting round turns something to face the other way
a thing not all there is incomplete, so only part of the words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Keith Moon, the famously wild Who drummer, was plainly mad and not quite right in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Round the twist and not all there both sound like British slang for crazy, which fits Moon's reputation; here they are working signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bono is the lead singer of the Irish band U2, one of the most famous rock musicians alive.

clue.text: Without a break paid for by revolutionary?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one after another, in succession
second meaning, whimsical: like 'on the house', charged to a Trotskyist

explanation.surface: A radical sponsor funds a nonstop run of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means consecutively; the question mark flags the jokey second reading, where a Trot is a Trotskyist and 'on the' means paid for by, as in 'on the house'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means consecutively, as in winning five games in a row, so it matches uninterrupted.

clue.text: High time to appear here?

parts.note: surface reading: it is about time something happened
setter's reading: the hour is shown high up on a tall building

explanation.walkthrough: 'High time' is an idiom for overdue, but read literally it is the time displayed high above a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure such as Big Ben carries a timepiece at its top, where the hours are literally shown up high.

clue.text: Drink fizzy tonic with, say, caviare reportedly

indicators.note: a fizzy liquid bubbles and churns, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: caviare is an example of fish roe; the French ending is pronounced the same way

explanation.surface: Serve a sparkling tonic alongside some caviar, a smart party order.
explanation.walkthrough: TONIC is rearranged to COINT, then comes the ending that sounds like ROE. 'Say' flags caviare as an example of roe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Manage each bad-tempered encounter

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
as in ten pence a head, meaning each
cross means angry or irritable

explanation.surface: Advice on handling every angry confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad-tempered encounter reads as a single phrase, but encounter is a verb standing alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is to meet them by chance, and encountering is chance meeting.

clue.text: Tried so desperately to get in my boss's position

indicators.note: acting desperately means flailing in all directions, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: An ambitious crossword setter scheming to take over the boss's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'my' is the setter speaking: a newspaper setter's boss is the editor, so the definition is that editor's job.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor runs a newspaper and commissions the crosswords, so the setter's superior holds the post of editor.

clue.text: Moon possibly more strange after onset of darkness

indicators.note: coming after means following behind, so this piece is placed second
the onset is the very beginning, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of darkness
rum means odd, so rummer is odder

explanation.surface: The moon seems stranger once night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: Moon is capitalised because it opens the clue, disguising Keith Moon, drummer of the Who. 'Possibly' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Moon played percussion for the rock band the Who, so he is one example of that kind of musician.

clue.text: Engineers riding express coach again

indicators.note: a rider sits on top, so in a down entry this piece comes first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
an express is a fast train

explanation.surface: Railway engineers catch an express and then board a coach again.
explanation.walkthrough: Express and coach both look like transport; coach is a verb in the definition, meaning teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to train or instruct someone, so coaching a second time is training anew.

clue.text: Pale moon obscured intermittently for long time

indicators.note: hidden at intervals, so every other letter is blanked and the rest kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A pale moon comes and goes behind the clouds for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The moon's light going on and off behind cloud is the picture; in the wordplay it is the letters themselves that come and go.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immeasurably long period, geological or figurative, so it equals an age.

clue.text: Buries cat beneath space by empty bins

indicators.note: being beneath in a down entry means coming lower, after the other piece

parts.note: an en is a printer's space
a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: emptying something takes out its contents, leaving only the outer shell

parts.note: the outside letters of bins

explanation.surface: Someone buries a dead cat in the gap beside some empty dustbins.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em, a common crossword source of EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, a way of interring the dead.

clue.text: Wine store missing the Spanish and French red

indicators.note: what is missing is absent, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: wine is kept in a cellar
el is Spanish for the
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A wine cellar has run out of Spanish and French reds.
explanation.walkthrough: CELLAR drops the E and L of EL, and ET is added. The Spanish and French look like nationalities of wine, not foreign words.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, and red is shorthand for red wine.

clue.text: Bear right, getting around a 180° turn first

indicators.note: to get around something is to go round the outside of it

parts.note: RT is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: coming first means placed at the front of the pair it belongs to

parts.note: a half-circle turn is a U-turn
as in ten miles an hour, a means per

explanation.surface: Driving directions: keep right and make a U-turn first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear right' reads as a driving instruction, but Bear is the definition. Rupert Bear is a long-running British children's comic-strip character in check trousers and scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is the famous cartoon bear of the Daily Express strip, so he is an example of a bear.

clue.text: Follower of Wigan or Oldham, but not Bolton?

definitions.text: Follower of Wigan or Oldham, but not Bolton?

parts.note: surface reading: a fan who supports one of these northern towns' teams
setter's reading: the word following these club names, whereas Bolton's club is Wanderers

explanation.walkthrough: Wigan and Oldham are Lancashire towns whose football clubs share a suffix; the nearby Bolton club is called Wanderers instead, so the word does not follow Bolton.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is literally the word that comes after the town name in two English football club titles.

clue.text: Dread tale about fallen leader drowning in loch

indicators.note: something drowning is submerged inside the water that surrounds it

parts.note: Loch Morar, in the western Highlands of Scotland, the deepest freshwater body in Britain

indicators.note: about means all around, in no fixed order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of fallen

explanation.surface: A frightening story about a toppled ruler who drowned in a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen leader' reads as a deposed ruler, but it only asks for the first letter of fallen. Loch Morar is a deep lake in the Scottish Highlands, less famous than Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortal fear is extreme terror, the kind felt for one's life, so as a noun it means dread.

clue.text: Low waning moon

indicators.note: waning means shrinking, so the word gets shorter by its final letter

parts.note: the satellite's name loses its final N

explanation.surface: A thin crescent moon sits low in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Low looks like an adjective for the moon's position, but it is a noun: the sound cattle make.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow lows, and its lowing is the sound written as a moo, so the noun is the call of cattle.

clue.text: Boldly attempt, without Yankee involvement, to reach moon

indicators.note: without means lacking, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: to try it on is to attempt something cheeky or audacious
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bold space mission to the moon, attempted without American involvement.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY IT ON loses its Y. Yankee suggests the Americans who went to the Moon, but it is just the phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune, and it is a natural satellite of that planet.

clue.text: Artists dropping by initially for long time devotees

indicators.note: dropping one thing for another means swapping it out for a replacement

parts.note: Cubists were painters such as Picasso and Braque

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letters are taken

parts.note: the first letter of by, which comes out
the first letters of long and time, which go in

explanation.surface: Painters who give up popping by, having been loyal followers for years.
explanation.walkthrough: In CUBISTS the B is swapped for LT. 'Initially' serves both 'by' and 'long time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultists are members of a cult, fervent followers of a person or creed, hence devotees.
